qt: to the Commission Isabella Tovaglieri (PfE), Silvia Sardone (PfE), Anna Maria Cisint (PfE), Susanna Ceccardi (PfE) Subject:

The Commission has introduced safeguard measures on imports of grain-oriented electrical steel (GOES), laminations, and magnetic cores, which will be in force until 26 February 2027. The Commission has stated that, in 2025, European producers held a 43% share of the GOES and SLC (slit laminations/cores) market. European manufacturers already incur costs that are 32-37 % higher than those of non-EU competitors. The Commission’s measures could increase the cost of lower-grade GOES by up to 100 %, result in smaller hikes for higher grades and also drive up the cost of cast-resin, distribution and power transformers by up to 60 %, 35 % and 20 % respectively. In the light of the above: 1.
On what grounds is the Commission basing its assessment that the benefits of these safeguard measures outweigh their repercussions for transformer manufacturers, jobs, competitiveness, and SMEs?

How does the Commission justify the fact that magnetic cores that are imported separately are treated differently to cores that are incorporated into imported transformers, and how does it intend to prevent this disparity from encouraging imports of finished transformers at the expense of European production?

Will the Commission review these measures before they expire to assess their impact on transformer manufacturers, and will it look into possible adjustments to address the rising volume of finished transformer imports?
